lead: Boston plumbing deals with old triple-deckers and brownstones, lead lines and hard New England winters. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Boston.
risk: lead and galvanized service lines, frozen pipes and old cast-iron stacks
risk_short: lead lines, frozen pipes and old pipes
why: Boston has one of the oldest housing stocks in the country. Triple-deckers in Dorchester and Jamaica Plain and brownstones in the South End often have galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and, in some cases, lead service lines.
Winter cold freezes pipes in exterior walls, porches and unheated basements. Multi-unit buildings share stacks, so one clog or leak can affect several homes.
water: Boston's water comes from the Quabbin and Wachusett reservoirs through the MWRA. It is soft. BWSC has a lead service line lookup and replacement program.
tips: Check BWSC's lead service line lookup.
Insulate pipes in exterior walls before winter.
Know where each unit's shutoff is in a multi-family home.
areas: PipeMend works in Back Bay, the South End, Dorchester, Jamaica Plain, South Boston, Charlestown, Roslindale and every other Boston neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Boston Inspectional Services Department, and plumbers must be licensed by the Massachusetts Board of State Examiners of Plumbers and Gas Fitters.

faq.q: Is Boston replacing lead water lines?
faq.a: Yes. The Boston Water and Sewer Commission has a lead service line program and an address lookup. It covers much of the cost of replacing the private side for eligible homes.
